Linesman in Phoney Business 
*262 DR. GOPALRAO VITHALRAO PATIL: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the news item 
captioned Linesman in "phoney' business published in the Indian Express 
dated the 4th December, 1999, regarding cheap calls abroad with the help of 
MTNL linesman; and 
(b) if so, what steps are being proposed to avoid such racket? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS (SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR): (a) and (b) A statement is 
laid on the Table of the House. 
9 

RAJYA SABHA [14 March, 2000] 
Statement 
(a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) The following steps have been taken to prevent recurrence:— 
 
— Prabhadevi Exchange, where the incident took place was of old 
technology (analog type). It has already been replaced by digital 
exchange. 
— Special surveillance is being maintained on such vulnerable 
exchanges. 
— The digital exchanges employ highly sophisticated signaling 
protocols which can not be simulated easily and als o there is no 
possibility for tapping individual junctions. 
— New technology Trunk Automatic Exchanges (Tax) have been 
installed which check the calling line identification and knock 
down the Tax call if it is directly originated from the junction. 
— As a prev entive measure, night inspections of Telephone 
Exchanges arc being conducted by Senior officers apart from 
officers of vigilance unit to check any possible misuse. 
— Dedicated CBI cells have been created in the four metros to detect 
and check telecom related frauds. 
— Strengthening of vigilance cells in ,the field units. 
DR. GOPALRAO VITHALRAO PATIL: Sir, some strange things are 
happening in the Telecom Department. Recently a CBI inquiry was ordered in 
one case. It was found that telephone lines at the Prabhadevi Exchange, which 
is the headquarters of MTNL at Mumbai, were being tapped. The CBI busted 
a racket. The CBI raided the house of a linemen and Rs.24 lakhs were seized 
from his possession. Some such things  are going on. I would like to know 
whether it was a fact and how it happened? 
SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR: Sir, it is a fact that Mr. C. Chandrashekhar, a 
phone mechanic in the Prabhadevi Exchange, Mumbai, has been arrested and 
Rs. 24.3 lakhs have been recovered from his residence alongwith his passport. 
A mobile telephone has also been recovered from his locker in the office. 
DR. GOPALRAO VITHALRAO PATIL: Sir, as we listened to the answer, 
we find that this is a very serious affair. This has a very different dimension. 
Here, 
10 

[14 March, 2000] RAJYA SABHA 
the underworld, working from Dubai and Karachi, is also involved. The 
person who had been arrested was hand -in-glove with the underworld, and all 
kinds of calls, whether ISD or STD, were made. The telephone lines had 
bypassed the exchange point and pulse code modulation system of the 
mainline. Ten telephone connection had been provided to these people. The 
Trunk Automatic Exchange was also bypassed. So, such serious things have 
been taking place. It has a security dimension. Terrorists are working against 
the cou ntry. So many things are happening in various cities, including 
Mumbai. I would like to know what steps the Government is taking to prevent 
such things. 
SHRI TAPAN SIKDAR: Yes, Sir, it is a matter of grave concern. Of 
course, these types of cases have been identified in other places also. So far as 
this case is concerned, three telephones, i.e. 4211668,4211670 and 4212831 
which were non-STD and non-ISD, were given ISD and STD facility through 
the Trunk Automatic Exchange by Mr. Chander Shekhar. Mr. Ram Shanker 
Yadav who is TTA has also been identified. Mr. Chander Shekhar is a phone 
mechanic. We have already taken some measures to control these things at the 
Prabha Devi Exchange. This was an old exchange, an analog type of 
exchange. This exchange has already  been upgraded as a modern digital 
exchange. This type of tapping work cannot be done through these modern 
exchanges, especially digital exchanges. This is my assurance to the House. 
Moreover, new technology Trunk Automatic Exchanges (TAX) have been 
installed which check the calling line identification and knock down the TAX 
call if it is directly originated from the junction. With this latest technology 
which is world -class technology, this type of work cannot be done in future. 
We have created more and mo re CBI cells to look into these things. Already, 
on the 9th of this month one man has been identified in Calcutta also. From 
there, Rs. 1,17,54,568 have been recovered. National Savings Certificates and 
other saving certificates worth Rs. 19,05,295 and gol d jewellery worth Rs. 
4,64,477 have been recovered. Sixteen bank accounts in different nationalized 
banks have been freezed. Keys of lockers have yet to be recovered. Bank 
balance of Rs. 3 lakhs and some movable households and other assets have 
already been detected. The CBI is taking stern action against them. I would

Medical Checkup of Cabin Crew 
1988. DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY: Will the Minister of CIVIL 
AVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that cabin crew are subjected to annual medical 
checkup without formulating compensation policy in the event of medical 
grounding; and 
(b) if so, whether such medical check-up is against the service rule? 
THE MINISTER OF CIVIL AVIATION (SHRI SHARAD YADAV): (a) 
and (b) As per Regulation 47 of Air India Employees se rvice regulations and 
secion 30 (c) and (d) of the standing orders, Female Cabin Crew (Air 
Hostesses) are required to undergo flying duties upto 35 years which may be 
extended to 50 years subject to their medical fitness for this purpose;. They are 
required to undergo biennial Medical examination after they attain 37 years of 
age upto 45 years of age and thereafter they are required to undergo medical 
examination on annual basis till they attain 50 years of age. A separate 
compensation policy in the form of annuity in the event of cabin crew being 
found medically unfit to perform duties of cabin Crew in set out in the 
Memorandum of Settlement of October 1972 signed between Air India and the 
then Air Corporation Employees Union. Male Cabin Crew are not required to 
undergo any corresponding medical examination because from the inception 
of service, the age of retirement of male Cabin Crew was 58 years without any 
question of an extention of service in their case. 
In Indian Airlines , Flying Cabin Crew are retained in the service of the 
Company so long as they remain medically fit for duties but are retired on 
attaining the medical examination once a year after attaining the age of 35 
years. There is also a Provisions for grant of ann uity for medically unfit Cabin 
Crew at variable rates which forms part of the settlement signed with the 
representative Union.

Companies Act, providing inter alia, that every company which accepts

company responsible for any contraventions of the provisions of the Act, and 
to provide that the small shareholders will have a right to elect at least one 
director in public companies. This Bill is currently before Parliament.

launched prosecution proceedings against 24 NBFCs and has filed police

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
BALASAHEB VIKHE PATIL): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) In formulating its fiscal policy the Government keeps in view the  
suggestions made by various professional/trade/business organisations. The  
Government recognise the need for imparting predictability in tax policy and  
policies are formulated keeping in view the economic situation and need for  
appropriate balance between revenue and expenditure consistent with policy  
objectives. On the taxation front the basic approach has been to move towards  
a tax structure which is simple, follows sound economic principles, relies on  
moderate tax rates and places emphasis on wider base and better 
enforcement. in Excise the task of convergence to a single rale of 16 per cent 
Central Value Added tax at the centre has been accomplished. This will 
encourage States to  implement their agreed programmes for converting their 
sales taxes into VAT  by 1.4.2001. Customs duty rates are being gradually 
phased down to bring  them broadly in line wit h Asian levels in a few years.

for corporate and personal  taxes. For medium term management of the fiscal 
deficit a committee has been  set up to examine and make suitable  
recommendations for a strong institutional mechanism embodied in a Fiscal 
Responsibility Act. For expenditure  management and restructuring an 
Expenditure Reforms Commission has been set up.

IMPORTANCE 
Situation arising out of mounting non-performing assets of banks 
SHRI GURUDAS DAS GUPTA (West Bengal): Sir, through this 
Calling Attention Notice, I call the attention of the hon. Minister of Finance to 
the situation arising out of the mounting non -performing assets (NPAs) of 
many of the public sector banks and the need for urgent steps for restoration 
of the health of such banks. 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI YASHWANT SINHA): Mr. 
Chairman, Sir, asset class ification and income recognition norms were 
initially     applied    to banking sector in   1992  and banks started asset  
172 

[14 March, 2000]             RAJYA SABHA 
classification and identification of NPAs on objective basis of defaults/record 
of recov ery from 1992- 93. After stabilization of identification norms and 
accounting of NPAs with concerted efforts over the period, the NPAs have 
been coming down in percentage terms. In percentage terms, gross NPAs 
which were 17.84 per cent of the total advances  as on 31.3.1997 have fallen 
to 15.89 per cent of total advances as on 31.3.1999. However, in absolute 
terms, the net NPAs of public sector banks have increased from Rs. 20285 
crore as on 31.3.1997 to Rs. 24211 crore as on 31.3.1999, while declining as 
a percentage of net advances from 9.18 per cent to 8.13 per cent during the 
same period. 
There are a number of factors for an asset turning into non-
performing. Some are internal, namely, wrong selection of project, deficient 
credit appraisal, managerial inef ficiency, lack of supervision by banks/FIs, 
lack of adequate, timely and continued support by the lending institutions and 
in some cases diversion and misutilisation of funds by the borrowers. 
However, a number of NPAs arise on account of external factors such as 
changes in policies, changes in technology rendering some products obsolete 
and some processes relatively costly, environmental concerns leading to 
decisions of Courts on relocation of industrial units and industry level factors 
such as cyclical downturn in some sectors. 
Having regard to the variety of reasons that had led to NPAs, the 
RBI and the Government as well as public sector banks have taken a number 
of steps not only to check the fresh incidence of NPAs but also to ensure the 
recovery of NP As. The steps taken by the Reserve Bank of India, 
Government of India and the public sector banks include the preparation of 
documents of loan recovery policy, reduction through negotiated settlement 
ensuring maximum recovery at minimum cost, strengthening  the Debt 
Recovery Tribunal mechanism, setting up of settlement advisory committee 
and focusing on recoveries by setting up recovery cells at Head Offices. 
In order to strengthen the Debt Recovery mechanism an Ordinance 
has been promulgated on 17.1.2000 to amend the Recovery of Debts due to 
Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993. I may add, as the Secretary -
General has said, that this has been passed by the other House and will be 
coming before this House. The Ordinance provides, inter alia, for set -off and 
counter claims, measures for prevention of alienation of property, 
appointment of receivers and commissioners by the Tribunals, appointment of 
172 

RAJYA SABHA [14 March, 2000] 
more than one recovery officer, and empowering the Tribunals to distribute  
the sale proceeds among secured creditors in accordance with the provisions 
of the Companies Act, 1956. In addition to DRTs and DRATs, which have 
either been set up or at an advanced stage of being set up, I propose to set up 
4 more DRTs in Mumbai and one each in Calcutta, Delhi and Chennai. 
Sharing of credit -related information on borrowers and potential 
borrowers is an input to improvement in credit decisions. A Credit 
Information Bureau to facilitate this is being set up. 
Banks as financial intermediari es are in a business activity that 
necessarily involves risks. The attempt has been, and must continue to be, to 
put in place systems that minimize risk, promote and create productive assets 
and increase profitability and viability of banks. Government is fully 
committed to providing credit support for agriculture, industry and business, 
while fully ensuring the soundness of financial system and good health of 
banks.

Comptroller and Auditor General, the RBI and the Government of India
